item.title: Posterior Cuff / Periscapular Soft-Tissue Mobilization
clinicalUse: Posterior shoulder muscle tenderness/guarding as an adjunct to active rehabilitation
patientPosition: Side-lying or prone with shoulder supported.
therapistPosition: Beside scapular region with relaxed shoulders/wrists.
stabilization: Arm and scapula supported so muscles can relax.
contact: Broad palm/thumb/forearm contact over posterior cuff/periscapular muscles, avoiding direct pressure on bony scapular borders.
forceDirection: Slow longitudinal or cross-fiber strokes within tolerance.
steps: 3. Focus on clinically relevant tender region.
safety: Avoid acute tear, bruising, open wound or unstable postoperative tissue.
item.visualCue: Broad posterior shoulder contact → slow tissue glide → re-test reach/rotation.

subTechniques.name: Pectoralis minor/major — Soft-Tissue Mobilization
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, side-lying or sitting with the arm supported.
subTechniques.contact: Broad hand/thumb/forearm contact over Pectoralis minor/major, avoiding nerves, vessels and painful bony prominences.
subTechniques.direction: Use longitudinal, transverse, kneading or sustained pressure matched to tissue orientation and tolerance.
subTechniques.dosage: Short-to-moderate bouts with frequent symptom checks.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
